references.title: (i) Astrometric kinematics: AGN are located at cosmological distances and are effectively stationary on the sky, exhibiting no measurable parallax or proper motion
iv) Cosmological distances: Multi-wavelength cross-matching with wide-area surveys (e.g. Cutri et al. (2021); Dark Energy Survey Collaboration et al.
(iii) Radio morphology: SFGs typically have angular sizes of ∼ 0 . 5–2 ′′ , with radio emission tracing the optical disc of the host galaxy
ii) Spectral behaviour: AGN typically exhibit smooth, power-law spectra ( 𝑆 𝜈 ∝ 𝜈 𝛼 ) governed by synchrotron emission processes (Kraus 1973)
iv) Polarisation: Negligible circular or linear polarisation, reflecting the incoherent aggregation of millions of independent, randomly oriented transmitters
ii) Spectral Shape: Stellar gyrosynchrotron emission typically displays a smooth, peaked spectrum (transitioning from optically thick to thin)
iv) Natural Emission: Since UCDs provide an astrophysical explanation for compact gigahertz radio emission
Propagation Effects: As true point sources
ii) Temporal Behaviour: Pulsars exhibit microsecond to millisec-ond pulse widths with extremely rigid periodicities ranging from milliseconds to seconds (Manchester et al. 2005)
(ii) Galactic kinematics: A local technosignature (10–100 pc) will probably be gravitationally bound to a nearby stellar system
